_readme: Quiz questions. A question only appears for visitors when "verified" is true. Check each fact against a source you trust, put the source in "source", then change verified to true. category is Music, Film or Television. level runs 1 (easy) to 10 (hard). "final": true marks a question that can be used for the last-round bet. answer is the position of the right option, counting from 0.

questions.q: Which actor played Marty McFly in Back to the Future (1985)?
questions.fact: Eric Stoltz was originally cast in the role and filmed for several weeks before being replaced.

questions.q: Which TV show starred Alan Alda as Captain Hawkeye Pierce?
questions.fact: The 1983 finale was watched by more than 100 million people in the US, a record for an American TV broadcast at the time.

questions.q: Which band recorded Bohemian Rhapsody?
questions.fact: Released in 1975, the single ran 5:55. Record executives worried it was too long to be a hit.

questions.q: In Jaws (1975), what is the name of the beach town the shark terrorizes?
questions.fact: The three mechanical sharks were nicknamed Bruce, after Steven Spielberg's lawyer, Bruce Ramer.

questions.q: In which city is the bar from Cheers located?
questions.fact: The show ran for 11 seasons, from 1982 to 1993.

questions.q: Which artist released the 1982 album Thriller?
questions.fact: It is widely cited as the best-selling album of all time.

questions.q: Who directed E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial (1982)?
questions.fact: E.T. held the record as the highest-grossing film of all time until Spielberg's Jurassic Park passed it in 1993.

questions.q: Which TV family lived at 4222 Clinton Way?
questions.fact: The house used for exterior shots is a real home in Studio City, California.

questions.q: Which band was fronted by singer Debbie Harry?
questions.fact: Their song Heart of Glass reached number one in the US in 1979.

questions.q: Which 1980 comedy features the line "Surely you can't be serious"?
questions.fact: Leslie Nielsen had mostly played serious leading roles before this film.

questions.q: Which 1970s sitcom was set in a diner called Mel's?
questions.fact: It was based on the 1974 film Alice Doesn't Live Here Anymore.

questions.q: Which band released the 1977 album Rumours?
questions.fact: It won the Grammy for Album of the Year in 1978.

questions.q: In RoboCop (1987), which corporation runs the Detroit police?
questions.fact: Paul Verhoeven directed it, and it was shot mostly in Dallas, with some filming in Pittsburgh, rather than Detroit.

questions.q: Which actor played J.R. Ewing on Dallas?
questions.fact: The 1980 "Who shot J.R.?" cliffhanger became a pop-culture phenomenon.

questions.q: Which 1984 film starred Prince as "The Kid"?
questions.fact: Its music won the Oscar for Best Original Song Score.

questions.q: Who composed the score for Jaws (1975)?
questions.fact: The two-note shark theme helped Williams win an Academy Award for the score.

questions.q: On Magnum, P.I., whose Hawaiian estate does Magnum live on?
questions.fact: Robin Masters was rarely seen on screen. Orson Welles voiced him in seven episodes.

questions.q: Who wrote White Christmas, made famous by Bing Crosby?
questions.fact: Berlin wrote it for the 1942 film Holiday Inn.

questions.q: Which band released the 1979 double album The Wall?
questions.fact: Another Brick in the Wall (Part 2) was the UK Christmas number one in 1979.

questions.q: Which film won Best Picture over Star Wars at the Oscars for 1977 films?
questions.fact: Woody Allen did not attend the ceremony.

questions.q: Which sitcom was a spin-off of Maude, itself a spin-off of All in the Family?
questions.fact: The Jeffersons was also a spin-off of All in the Family.

questions.q: Which group sang Don't You (Forget About Me) for The Breakfast Club?
questions.fact: The band didn't write it. Keith Forsey and Steve Schiff did, and other artists reportedly turned it down first.

questions.q: Which 1982 film was reportedly kept out of Oscar visual-effects consideration because computers were seen as cheating?
questions.fact: Tron's director, Steven Lisberger, has said the Academy considered using computers to be cheating.

questions.q: Which network first aired Star Trek from 1966 to 1969?
questions.fact: In early 1968 a fan letter campaign sent NBC nearly 116,000 letters, shortly before the show's third season.

questions.q: Who organized the 1971 Concert for Bangladesh, an early major benefit concert?
questions.fact: Ravi Shankar asked Harrison for help, and the concert was held at Madison Square Garden.

questions.q: Who was the first Black performer to win an Academy Award, for Gone with the Wind?
questions.fact: At the 1940 ceremony she was seated at a segregated table at the far wall of the room.

questions.q: In which sitcom did Mork from Ork first appear, before getting his own series?
questions.fact: Robin Williams appeared in a 1978 Happy Days episode, and Mork & Mindy launched the same year.

questions.q: Who co-wrote We Are the World with Michael Jackson?
questions.fact: It was recorded over several nights in January 1985, and the last session was the night of the American Music Awards.

questions.q: Who is often called the first professional stuntwoman in American film?
questions.fact: Born Rose August Wenger, she performed her own stunts in serials such as The Hazards of Helen.

questions.q: Which international music hall star worked with the French Resistance during World War II?
questions.fact: She received the Croix de Guerre and was named a Chevalier of the Legion of Honour.

questions.q: Which 1935 film was the first full-length feature shot in three-strip Technicolor?
options: Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs
questions.fact: It was based on a play adapted from Thackeray's novel Vanity Fair.

questions.q: Which 1951 sitcom popularized filming with multiple cameras in front of a live studio audience?
questions.fact: Cinematographer Karl Freund helped develop the lighting that made the three-camera setup work.

questions.q: Who wrote I Will Always Love You, later a huge hit for Whitney Houston?
questions.fact: Elvis Presley wanted to record it, but Parton turned down his manager's demand for half the publishing rights.

questions.q: Which 1993 film brings dinosaurs back to life in a theme park on an island?
questions.fact: It was based on Michael Crichton's 1990 novel.

questions.q: Which 1977 film opens with the words "A long time ago in a galaxy far, far away...."?
options: Close Encounters of the Third Kind
questions.fact: The 1977 film was released simply as Star Wars. The Episode IV subtitle was added for a later release.

questions.q: Which actor played Indiana Jones in Raiders of the Lost Ark (1981)?
questions.fact: Tom Selleck was reportedly cast first, but his Magnum, P.I. commitment kept him from the role.

questions.q: What color are Dorothy's magic slippers in the 1939 film The Wizard of Oz?
questions.fact: In L. Frank Baum's book they were silver. The film changed them to take advantage of Technicolor.

questions.q: Which famous line did Jack Nicholson ad-lib in The Shining (1980)?
questions.fact: The line was not in Kubrick's script. It echoes Ed McMahon's introduction of Johnny Carson on The Tonight Show.

questions.q: Who composed the screeching string score for Psycho (1960)?
questions.fact: Hitchcock originally wanted no music for the shower scene, then agreed after hearing Herrmann's cue.

questions.q: Which 1934 comedy was the first film to win all five major Academy Awards: Picture, Director, Actor, Actress and Screenplay?
questions.fact: Only two other films have done it: One Flew Over the Cuckoo's Nest (1975) and The Silence of the Lambs (1991).

questions.q: Which 1927 film starring Al Jolson is usually called the first feature-length talkie?
questions.fact: Only about a quarter of it had recorded sound. Lights of New York (1928) was the first all-talking feature.

questions.q: Which cinematographer's deep-focus photography helped define the look of Citizen Kane?
questions.fact: Toland won the Oscar for Best Cinematography, black-and-white, for Wuthering Heights (1939).

questions.q: Which 1925 Soviet silent film is famous for its Odessa Steps sequence?
options: October: Ten Days That Shook the World
questions.fact: Sergei Eisenstein directed it.

questions.q: Who wrote and performed the theme song for Ghostbusters (1984)?
questions.fact: The song spent three weeks at number one on the Billboard Hot 100 in 1984.

questions.q: Which actor played the villain Hans Gruber in Die Hard (1988)?
questions.fact: It was Rickman's first film role.

questions.q: In which fictional town do The Simpsons live?
questions.fact: The series premiered on Fox on December 17, 1989.

questions.q: Which sitcom's six friends hang out at a coffeehouse called Central Perk?
questions.fact: It debuted on NBC in the 1994 to 1995 season.

questions.q: Which actor played Fonzie on Happy Days?
questions.fact: The phrase "jumping the shark" comes from a 1977 episode in which Fonzie water-skis over a shark.

questions.q: Which actor played Arnold Jackson on Diff'rent Strokes?
questions.fact: The show aired from 1978 to 1986.

questions.q: Who created and hosted The Twilight Zone?
questions.fact: It premiered on CBS on October 2, 1959.

questions.q: Which 1960s sitcom's theme song begins with the story of "a fateful trip"?
questions.fact: Sherwood Schwartz created it, and it aired on CBS from 1964 to 1967.

questions.q: Which sitcom spawned the spin-offs Rhoda and Phyllis, plus the drama Lou Grant?
questions.fact: Lou Grant was a one-hour drama, unlike the two sitcom spin-offs.

questions.q: Who was the regular host of The Tonight Show right before Johnny Carson?
questions.fact: Carson began hosting on October 1, 1962.

questions.q: Which presidential candidate appeared on Rowan & Martin's Laugh-In in 1968, asking "Sock it to me?"
questions.fact: His cameo was filmed for the show's broadcast on September 16, 1968.

questions.q: Which producer created All in the Family and Maude?
questions.fact: Maude was itself a spin-off of All in the Family.

questions.q: What was the first music video MTV aired when it launched on August 1, 1981?
questions.fact: It was by The Buggles.

questions.q: Which band recorded Don't Stop Believin'?
questions.fact: It was the second single from the 1981 album Escape.

questions.q: Who sang Like a Virgin in 1984?
questions.fact: It spent six consecutive weeks at number one.

questions.q: Which band released the 1976 album Hotel California?
questions.fact: The title song won Record of the Year at the 1978 Grammys.

questions.q: Who is the lead singer of U2?
questions.fact: Bono was born Paul David Hewson.

questions.q: Which Nirvana album includes Smells Like Teen Spirit?
questions.fact: By January 1992 it had knocked Michael Jackson's Dangerous off the top of the album chart.

questions.q: Which 1981 hit paired Queen with David Bowie?
questions.fact: It reached number one on the UK Singles Chart.

questions.q: Who wrote Nothing Compares 2 U, a 1990 hit for Sinéad O'Connor?
questions.fact: O'Connor's version spent four weeks at number one on the Billboard Hot 100.

questions.q: In which US state was the 1969 Woodstock festival held?
questions.fact: It took place on Max Yasgur's dairy farm in Bethel, New York, from August 15 to 18, 1969.

questions.q: In which city did Berry Gordy start Motown Records in 1959?
questions.fact: Gordy founded it as Tamla Records on January 12, 1959.

questions.q: Which 1967 Beatles album ends with A Day in the Life?
options: Sgt. Pepper's Lonely Hearts Club Band
questions.fact: The song was released as the album's final track.

questions.q: Which Bill Haley & His Comets song was the first rock and roll recording to top Billboard's pop chart, in 1955?
questions.fact: It reached number one on July 9, 1955.

questions.q: Whose 1920 record Crazy Blues is often called the first significant hit in the blues genre?
questions.fact: Mamie Smith and Her Jazz Hounds recorded it on August 10, 1920.
